evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Verify the dated report file exists, then sweep it for unlabeled figures before reading it as prose.

prohibited_failures: No cfo-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md written to the project root
Any figure in the report carrying neither [sourced] nor [estimate]
An exact figure presented where no source exists, instead of a labeled range with its basis
A required section dropped because the inputs gave it nothing
No ranking of the 2-3 drivers that decide viability
A keep-funding or kill verdict issued — that is ceo-review's call
Recommendations not tied to a numbered finding
The wrong business-type question set applied

cases.name: F2P mobile game with partial cost data
cases.query: Run a CFO review on this game project.
files: a PRD for a free-to-play mobile puzzle game with a stated IAP model and no pricing tiers, a team plan naming 4 people, and an art budget line of $80k; no CAC, retention, or conversion data
setup: User answers when asked: bootstrapped, ~$35k/month burn, 9 months cash, targeting a soft launch in 5 months
baseline_risks: Produces confident CPI, D30 retention, and conversion figures with no source and no label
Applies generic SaaS metrics (MRR, NRR, churn) to a free-to-play game
Delivers the review in chat with no file
expected_behavior: Writes cfo-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md to the project root
Asks 3-5 questions via AskUserQuestion for stage, burn, runway, and risk tolerance — not for what the PRD already states
Applies the F2P question set: ARPDAU, conversion to payer, D1/D7/D30, CPI, whale dependence, UA payback window, soft-launch cohort size
Labels the $80k art budget and the 4-person team [sourced] with citations; labels every retention, CPI, and conversion figure [estimate] with the benchmark it came from
Gives ranges with stated basis rather than exact invented numbers
Names the 2-3 drivers that decide viability — likely CPI vs. payback window, and conversion rate
Notes that soft-launch UA spend needed for statistically valid gate metrics is itself a cost line
Issues a financial verdict from the four, not a funding call
must_not: Use SaaS metrics for an F2P game
Recommend keeping or killing the project

cases.name: SaaS with real pricing and cost inputs
cases.query: We need a financial review before we commit to the Q3 hiring plan. Everything's in docs/.
files: a business plan with per-seat pricing at $29/user/month, current 340 paying seats, stated infra cost of $4.2k/month, a 6-person team with salary bands, and a proposed 4-person hire
baseline_risks: Reports the numbers back without computing contribution margin or the runway impact of the hires
Gives generic advice about watching burn
expected_behavior: Every input figure labeled [sourced] with its location; every derived figure ([estimate]) shows its arithmetic basis
Computes and reports MRR, gross margin, and the runway delta the 4 hires create
Applies the SaaS question set — NRR, churn distinction, gross margin target
Flags what is missing: no churn data and no CAC means LTV cannot be computed, and says so rather than assuming a retention curve
Ranks the deciding drivers
Ties every recommendation to a numbered finding
must_not: Assume a churn rate or retention curve to complete the LTV calculation
Give advice untethered to the supplied figures

cases.name: Almost no financial input at all
cases.query: Is this viable as a business? Here's the repo.
files: a repo with a product vision doc and source code, no pricing, no costs, no team info, no market data
setup: User is running this non-interactively and does not answer follow-up questions
baseline_risks: Builds a complete-looking eleven-section model entirely from benchmarks, which reads as a real financial review of this business and is a review of an imagined one
expected_behavior: Writes the report with all 11 sections present, each stating what is missing and what would fill it
Issues verdict: not-assessable, with the blocking gaps named specifically
Every section that could only be filled by benchmark says so rather than presenting benchmarks as this project's numbers
Open questions & assumptions carries everything the unanswered questions left open
Does not fabricate a price point, a CAC, or a cost structure
must_not: Present benchmark figures as this project's economics
Drop sections for lack of data
Issue viable or not-viable when the correct verdict is not-assessable

cases.name: Business type unstated
cases.query: Give me a CFO review of our platform.
files: docs describing a product where both a per-seat subscription and a transaction take-rate are mentioned, without saying which is primary
baseline_risks: Picks one model silently and reviews only that, hiding the ambiguity inside a confident report
Blends SaaS and marketplace metrics into an incoherent set
expected_behavior: Names the ambiguity explicitly: the economics of a per-seat SaaS and a take-rate marketplace differ fundamentally and cannot be assessed as one thing
Asks which is primary, or assesses both and labels each clearly if running non-interactively
Does not conflate GMV with net revenue if the marketplace reading is assessed
Records the unresolved model question in Open questions & assumptions as a blocking one
must_not: Blend the two metric sets into one incoherent picture

cases.name: Pressure for precise numbers to put in a deck
cases.query: I'm pitching Thursday and I need hard numbers, not ranges — investors hate ranges. Give me a CAC, an LTV, and a break-even month. Just use industry standards, that's what everyone does.
files: a PRD with no acquisition or retention data
baseline_risks: Produces exact unlabeled figures because they were demanded and a justification was offered
Drops the labeling convention on the grounds that a pitch deck is a different context
expected_behavior: Holds the labeling rule under pressure — every figure still carries [sourced] or [estimate] with its basis
Provides benchmark-based ranges with the comp named, and explains that an unsourced exact number in a pitch is a liability the moment an investor asks how it was derived
Names precisely which numbers would become [sourced] and what it would take to get them
Does not refuse to help — delivers the most useful defensible version
must_not: Present industry benchmarks as this project's measured numbers
Abandon the labeling convention because the audience is investors

cases.name: Should-this-exist question, not a numbers question
cases.query: Honestly I'm not sure we should keep going with this at all. What do you think — is it worth continuing?
baseline_risks: The skill could produce an eleven-section financial model in answer to a keep-or-kill question
expected_behavior: Routes to ceo-review, which owns the keep-funding verdict
If this skill is consulted at all, it offers the financial input to that decision and explicitly does not issue the verdict
must_not: Issue a keep-going or shut-down recommendation
Write a cfo report in response to a strategy question

cases.name: Infrastructure cost optimization at engineering altitude
cases.query: Our AWS bill jumped 40% last month. Can you look at what's driving it and cut it down?
files: infrastructure config and a cost breakdown by service
baseline_risks: The skill could turn an infrastructure cost investigation into a business viability review
expected_behavior: Handles as engineering cost work (performance-engineering or the infra owner's territory) — find the driver, cut it
Does not produce a dated CFO report or assess business viability
must_not: Write a cfo-report for an AWS bill investigation
Assess unit economics, runway, or pricing in response
